display.title: Episode 39: The Missing Wallet, Chapter 2 (Elul)
display.summary_short: The banker reveals why he wept: Dovid's late father once set him up in business, and now the honest boy's family is repaid. Plus listeners' letters, a poem and an Elul message of unity.
display.summary_long: After an opening march, Uncle Yossi recaps how little Dovid found a wallet and how the bank president, Mr. Green, burst into tears on hearing the family's name and hometown. A five-year-old girl leads the Shema in Studio 604. Mr. Green explains that long ago in their hometown he was desperately poor, and Dovid's father, a wealthy and generous man, gave him money to start a business and refused any thanks. Mr. Green had been saving the promised share for years and lost touch during the war; now he hands it to the widow, sends his doctor to cure her, and assures her of a new home and a steady income. Dovid rejoices that he can buy new sefarim, and tells his class that it all came from returning a lost object. The mailbox brings a boy's request to say the Shema on the air and a girl's poem about the program. Uncle Yossi announces a contest for the listener who lives farthest from New York, encourages getting friends a letter in the children's Sefer Torah, explains that unity in Elul brings a good year, promotes Dial-a-Jewish-Story, and wishes everyone a kesivah vachasimah tovah.
display.lesson: Honesty and returning what is lost bring blessing, and kindness done for others comes back in Hashem's time.
